newsitem.title: USA: AK Steel union seeks Middletown expansion.
newsitem.headline: AK Steel union seeks Middletown expansion.

text.p: Workers at AK Steel Holding Corp's Middletown, Ohio, plant want the company to locate the steel processing plant it is planning at the site of its present plant, union officials told analysts Wednesday.

AK Steel has announced that it is considering construction of an entirely new "world class" cold strip mill facility, explained Michael Bailey, president of the Armco Employees Independent Federation.
Although AK Steel has not announced where the new facility will be built, the company has applied for environmental permits in areas near Rockport, Ind., and Columbus, Ohio.
AK spokesman Alan McCoy acknowledged the company has applied for the permits, calling this "part of the modeling work" for one alternative -- new construction.
"Our message is very simple: AK Steel should consider a very reasonable and prudent alternative, expand in Middletown," Bailey said.

Citing newspaper reports that the plant will cost some $1.1 billion, the Union released a five-page position paper asserting the Middletown Works has more than enough land, adequate resources and utilities as well as an infrastructure that will save millions on both construction and operations.
Bailey represents 3,300 workers at the Middletown Works. He was accompanied by Middletown community representatives.
They called on AK Steel shareholders to encourage the company to commission an independent feasibility study to determine the best location for a major expansion.

"The members we represent fear for their jobs. They fear for their futures, and the future of their families," Bailey explained. "That fear is made worse by AK Steel's reluctance to discuss these issues with us" or other community leaders.
He said "the company never even sat down and explained why it has considered locating the new facility outside of Middletown."
Baily said the union is calling for an independent feasibility study for submission to investors to evaluate the advantages of locating a new cold mill complex at Middletown.

He said such a study would compare capital costs, operating costs, environmental impacts and balance sheet implications; and called for it to be immediately conducted so that a report could be made to shareholders within 60 days.
Asked about the study and other comments at the New York presentation, McCoy said "we continue to have no comment."
